clue.text: One over-indulger embracing another in tap

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold something within your arms, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard, one who over-indulges in drink
a pig is another kind of over-indulger, a glutton

explanation.surface: A drunk is pictured hugging a fellow glutton in a bar, or in a taproom.
explanation.walkthrough: One over-indulger is a whole phrase for the first piece; another names a second, different kind of over-indulger.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a peg or valve controlling flow from a cask, i.e. a kind of tap.

clue.text: Church yard under rocks making a harsh sound

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under something means coming after it in the written word

parts.note: scree is loose broken rock on a mountain slope
CH is the standard abbreviation for church
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A churchyard set beneath a rocky slope gives out a grating noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Screechy means shrill and grating, an adjective describing something making a harsh sound.

clue.text: Emblems and one name dropped from pub marker, I admitted initially

indicators.note: something dropped from a word is taken out of it, so a letter goes missing

parts.note: an inn sign marks a pub
N is the abbreviation for name; one of the two Ns goes
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the first letter of admitted

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to removing a name from a pub's signboard and keeping the emblems.
explanation.walkthrough: INN SIGN has two Ns, and dropping one leaves INSIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are badges or distinguishing marks of office, which are emblems.

clue.text: Chamber piece? Some Schubert etc obviously turns up here

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters read from bottom to top
some of the following words means only a part of their run of letters is used

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of Schubert, all of etc and the start of obviously

explanation.surface: A listener remarks that a chamber work by Schubert or similar composers naturally shows up here.
explanation.walkthrough: Schubert famously wrote an Octet, so the surface is apt as well as the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a composition for eight players, a typical piece of chamber music; the question mark marks the punning sense.

clue.text: Mean to restrict a lot of fantastic YA book series?

indicators.note: restricting something means hemming it in, so one word is held inside the other

parts.note: tight means stingy, mean with money

indicators.note: a lot of a word is most but not all of it, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: wild can mean fantastic or extravagant

explanation.surface: A grumpy critic wants to cut back an overblown series of young-adult novels.
explanation.walkthrough: YA means young adult, the publishing category for teenage readers.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is Stephenie Meyer's vampire saga, an example of a young-adult book series, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Meteorologist recreates thaw after storm

indicators.note: after a storm everything is tossed about and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A forecaster explains that the thaw returns once the storm has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: A weathercaster presents weather forecasts, and in loose usage is a meteorologist.

clue.text: Depression after network shows farmer, perhaps

indicators.note: after places the first-named part later in the word than the second

parts.note: LAN is a local area network
a downer is a depressing experience or a low mood

explanation.surface: A rural worker is seen feeling low after spending time online.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer who owns his acres is an example of a landowner, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Man that's kept programmer's mantra — look!

parts.note: GIGO stands for garbage in, garbage out, a computing maxim
lo is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: A coder repeats a favourite saying and calls for attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a man supported financially by a lover, a kept man.

clue.text: Expression of annoyance initially over red socks and trainers

parts.note: tut is a clicking sound of disapproval

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the next few words

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone tuts at a person in red socks paired with sports shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: Trainers are sports shoes in British English, which is what the surface wants you to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutors teach and coach pupils, so they are trainers in the sense of instructors.

clue.text: Support adopting end to futile return to first principles

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one word takes another inside it

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a cue or an arm

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of futile

explanation.surface: Backing a doomed effort, someone decides to go back to basics.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset is to restore to an initial state, going back to the starting position.

clue.text: Childish game, note, adopted by a good many men having fun

indicators.note: being adopted by something means being taken into it, so these go inside

parts.note: a sight is informal for a great deal, as in a sight better
tag is the playground chasing game
N is short for note

explanation.surface: A crowd of men amusing themselves by playing a playground game.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag night is a pre-wedding party for the groom and his male friends, an occasion of men enjoying themselves.

clue.text: Streets around Essex town — one contribution to river crossing

indicators.note: around places the outer word on both sides of the inner one

parts.note: ST is short for street, and two are needed
Epping is a town in Essex, England
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Essex town's streets play a part in getting across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural Streets supplies ST twice, one on each side of EPPING.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepping stone is one of a line of stones used to cross a stream, so it contributes to a crossing.

clue.text: the i repeatedly upset about Guardian leader? Just a fraction

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters go around the next piece
upset signals the doubled letters are knocked over into a new order
repeatedly tells us the words the i are used twice over
leader picks the first letter of Guardian

explanation.surface: A jibe that the i newspaper keeps tying itself in knots over a Guardian editorial, though it is a small matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British newspaper. 'upset' rearranges THEITHEI into EIHTIETH, and 'about' puts G, the first letter of Guardian, inside after EI.
explanation.definitionFit: One part in eighty is a tiny share of a whole, merely a small fraction.

clue.text: I heard you will dismiss first Rector about student one's observed rudely

definitions.note: read as one who has observed rudely

indicators.note: about means going round, so the shortened word encloses the next
to dismiss the first is to send away the opening letter

parts.note: radio operators say roger to mean message received
R is short for rector; it is the letter dismissed
L is a learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A radio voice warns that a rector will be sent away for some rude behaviour towards a student.
explanation.walkthrough: ROGER loses its first R, the Rector, leaving OGER, which wraps round L.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogler is someone who stares at others lecherously, a rude way of looking.

clue.text: A lot about one King and father, perhaps — to me?

definitions.note: read as a king speaking of his successor

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round what follows

parts.note: a heap is a large amount
the Roman numeral for one
R is for rex, Latin for king
a father is one example of a parent

explanation.surface: A monarch, who is also a father, muses about his successor.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the monarch's own voice: to a king, the heir apparent is the one next in line after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The heir apparent is the person certain to inherit a throne, so a king asks who stands in that relation to him.

clue.text: Apparently a renegade American device

parts.note: app. is a dictionary abbreviation for apparently
taken as written
a rat is a deserter or turncoat
US is short for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a defector from the States has some sort of gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is equipment or machinery for a task, a device.

clue.text: 'Rail' is seen in 'raillery'

indicators.note: something seen in another thing sits inside it

parts.note: raillery is good-humoured teasing, banter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wordplay remark: the word rail can be found inside the word raillery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at a literal hidden word, since rail does appear in raillery, but that is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A banister is the handrail running up a staircase, a kind of rail.

clue.text: Rash behaviour still on the rise around desert

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first word goes about the second
in a down clue, rising means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: yet means still, as in not yet done
desert means what one deserves, so merit

explanation.surface: Reckless conduct is still increasing in a desert region.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert here is the noun from deserve, as in just deserts, not the sandy place.
explanation.definitionFit: Temerity is reckless boldness, so rash behaviour fits as a noun phrase.

clue.text: Unconventional ménage — or pair in this?

definitions.text: Unconventional ménage — or pair in this?

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, ignoring the accent

explanation.surface: An unusual household, or a couple living a particular arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: an unconventional household, or a couple, might be in such an arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An open marriage lets both spouses have other partners, an unconventional domestic arrangement for a couple.

clue.text: Vital stuff — noodle soup — for poet

parts.note: sap is the life fluid of a plant, and vigour
pho is Vietnamese noodle soup

explanation.surface: A bowl of noodle soup is recommended as nourishment for a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho was the ancient Greek lyric poet of Lesbos.

clue.text: Second tee: top player adopting new address

parts.note: S is short for second
tee is how the letter T is spelt out

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the word takes the next letter inside

parts.note: an ace is an expert player
N is short for new

explanation.surface: On the second tee, a top golfer settles into a fresh position to hit the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf scene is the decoy: tee only spells the letter, though address is also golf language for preparing to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, to address the ball is to take up one's stance, so stance and address are synonyms here.

clue.text: Editor 'outing' Communist performer

indicators.note: outing here means putting out or expelling, so letters are removed

parts.note: a redactor is an editor
red is a common term for a communist

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor exposes a left-wing entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: Outing suggests revealing someone, but it means throwing RED out of REDACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is a stage or screen performer.

clue.text: Gloomy function bringing in a performer

indicators.note: bringing in means taking something inside, so the first word holds the rest

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
taken as written
a turn is a music-hall act or performer

explanation.surface: A dull social occasion livened up by hiring an entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: Function pretends to be a party, but it is the maths kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a gloomy, sullen temperament, traditionally linked to the planet Saturn.

clue.text: After upset, rower keeping it in proportion

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards
keeping means holding inside, so the word takes the next one in

parts.note: an oar can mean an oarsman, a rower
taken as written

explanation.surface: A capsized rower tries to keep things in perspective.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is the quantitative relation between two amounts, i.e. their proportion.

clue.text: Continue to run amok, returning after detective apprehends Nationalist or Red

indicators.note: after places the reversed phrase behind the next part

parts.note: PI is a private investigator

indicators.note: to apprehend is to seize and hold, so a letter is taken inside
returning means going back, so the phrase is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to riot on is to keep running riot
N is short for Nationalist

explanation.surface: A sleuth arrests either a nationalist or a communist rioter.
explanation.walkthrough: Red looks like the communist in a political pairing with Nationalist, but it is the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot noir is a grape and the red wine made from it, so a red.

clue.text: Something for everyone? Three times I must secure lowest cinema classification

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast inside, so one letter goes within

parts.note: T is short for time, so three of them
U, for universal, is the least restrictive British film certificate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film fan insists, again and again, on getting the mildest certificate so everyone can watch.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is a musical direction or passage for all performers together, so a part for everyone.

clue.text: Poet's completed penning poem — I should check

indicators.note: penning means writing in or enclosing, so one word goes inside

parts.note: o'er is the poetic contraction of over, meaning finished
a verse is a poem

explanation.surface: A poet's finished writing, and someone says they should check it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the voice of the answer: an overseer could say this of himself.
explanation.definitionFit: An overseer supervises and checks others' work, so checking is the job.

clue.text: Outlaw to plunder King, say, almost entirely escaping

parts.note: to rob is to plunder

indicators.note: what escapes from a word gets away from it, so those letters vanish

parts.note: a king is an example of a royal
entirely is ALL, and almost drops its last letter

explanation.surface: A bandit plans to rob the king, and nearly gets away with it.
explanation.walkthrough: Rob Roy MacGregor was an 18th-century Scottish outlaw and folk hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Rob Roy is famous as a Highland outlaw, so the name stands for one.
